transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I don't want to waste your time, but... well, I wanted to talk about a little trouble I've been having at work. 

I'm an auditor, and usually I'm really on top of things, I promise. But what finally pushed me to make this appointment is that I keep starting these follow-up items after my audits, or sometimes after mentorship events. And I sit down with every intention of finishing them right then and there. But then I'll find out, like, days later, that the final email, or a review note, or a sign-off form just... never actually got done. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really do care about my work and I don't want people to think I'm slacking off. Is that... is that the kind of thing I should be bringing up here? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you been noticing these difficulties with following through and finishing tasks?

Um, well... I guess it's been about a year and ten months? Almost two years, give or take. 

I was actually doing really well before that, I promise. I had even won this firm-wide award, which was really wonderful, and they promoted me right after. But, um... with the promotion came a lot more responsibilities. And I am so, so grateful for the opportunity, I really am! It's just... the workload got a little bit harder to juggle, and I think that's when I started noticing these little slip-ups with finishing things. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I can't handle my job, or that I'm complaining about the promotion. I really do try my best to keep everything running smoothly. Does that timeline make sense for what you're looking for?
Thinking back to your childhood or school years, did you ever struggle with focus, organization, or finishing tasks back then?

Oh, um... childhood? Gosh, I, well... I was always a really good student, honestly! I loved school and I caught on to things pretty quickly. 

But, um, I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid, because I really wasn't—there were a few little things. Like, my elementary school teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, but... maybe a little too eager? Like I would talk out of turn sometimes, just because I was so excited to participate. And they'd mention that I might rush past some of the smaller details, or that I needed a gentle reminder here and there to actually finish my work instead of moving on to the next fun thing. 

I did misplace an assignment or two, but I always meant well! My mother actually still teases me about it. She jokes that I could get an A on a test, but completely forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. 

It was never anything terrible, I promise. Just... typical kid stuff, right? I hope that's the kind of information you were asking for?
Do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you have an internal motor that makes it difficult to sit still?

Um, well... I guess I do get a little fidgety sometimes? But not in a disruptive way, I promise! I don't want to make it sound like I'm bouncing off the walls or anything. 

It's just... sometimes when I have to sit still for a really long review at work, it starts to feel a bit... physically uncomfortable? Almost like there's this little bit of pressure building up inside me. And I just get this overwhelming urge to move. 

But I always try to handle it professionally! I'll just, you know, stand up and walk to the printer, or maybe invent a quick reason to go check on something across the office. Just to stretch my legs a bit. I think everyone gets a little restless during long meetings, right? I hope that doesn't sound too unusual... is that the sort of thing you meant?
In conversations or meetings at work, do you often find yourself blurting out answers or interrupting others before they finish speaking?

Oh, gosh... um, well... I really try my best to be a good listener, I promise. I know how important it is to let everyone have their say, especially in a professional setting. 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, I do sometimes catch myself... maybe jumping in a little too early? Especially when I'm working with the junior auditors. It's never because I want to be rude or talk over them! It's just... sometimes an idea or the answer to what they're asking just pops into my head, and it feels so... urgent? Like I just have to get it out right that second, and I kind of blurt it out before I can even stop myself. 

I always apologize right after, though! I really don't want them to think I don't value their input. It's just that my brain gets a little too far ahead of the conversation sometimes. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible manager... does that make sense?

She demonstrates persistent symptoms of inattention (failure to follow through and complete routine work tasks, careless omissions of details) alongside hyperactivity and impulsivity (inner restlessness, urge to move during prolonged sitting, blurting out answers, and interrupting colleagues).
